newsitem.title: GERMANY: INSTANT VIEW - Dec Ifo business climate index.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Dec Ifo business climate index.

text.p: Following are reactions from economists to a report from the Ifo economics research institute that its west German business climate index fell to 95.8 from 96.9 in December

HANS-JUERGEN MELTZER, DEUTSCHE BANK: There were two to three fewer working days (in December). That might explain the lower number. But there will still be a modest recovery in the economy. For the time being there will not be a cut in the repo rate, but pressure may mount. January could be distorted lower by seasonal effects. The Bundesbank will not cut because it may disturb the bond market.

HANS GUENTHER RAEDEKER, CHASE MANHATTEN, LONDON: "We expected a number slightly above 96, so we are not too surprised about this low number. We have seen weak economic data recently and the sentiment in the economy has changed dramatically. Also, other surveys have indicated that already. The ifo index always has been above other indicators.

In the near future the economy will be boosted by a favourable dollar/mark exchange rate. Especially the export sector will profit from that. All in all, however, the recovery will be less pronounced than many people have been expecting. Unemployment will continue to be high.

The Bundesbank will hold rates on hold and will wait for the impact of a strong Dollar on the economy first. From March onwards, however, we do expect a decline in the repo rate and later possibly even in the key interest rates.

STEFAN SCHNEIDER, ECONOMIST, BANQUE PARIBAS CAPITAL MANAGEMENT, Frankfurt: The drop in Ifo business climate index is largely due to cold weather. Especially the construction sector took a downturn and brought the overall index lower. This weather effect will taper off in March or April, however. At that time then the favourable exchange rate situation will have a more distinctive impact on the economic situation.

Pressure on the Bundesbank is increasing, also since the government finds itself in a straight jacket. Yet, the Bundesbank won't move soon. Bund yields could fall further in the short term. I believe 5.50 percent is possible. Yet, we are not looking at a recession. So, I am positive on Bunds for the next six to eight weeks, but after that yields will come up again.
